New York marks 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks. New York commemorated the 25th anniversary of the devastating attacks of September 11, 2001 on Friday with a ceremony marred by controversy over President Donald Trump’s absence, and right-wing outrage over the attendance of the city’s first Muslim mayor. In an unusual move, Trump paid his respects at the Pentagon, rather than joining the event in New York, where hijacked planes destroyed the World Trade Centre and killed most of the 2,977 total victims on that world-altering day. Vice President JD Vance and Trump’s four living predecessors — Republican George W. Bush, who was in office during the attacks, and Democrats Joe Biden, Barack Obama and Bill Clinton — were gathering at the Ground Zero site in lower Manhattan. The ceremony, which began just after 8:40am (5:40pm PKT), was designed to be apolitical, with no speeches. (From L to R) Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, former US president Bill Clinton, former first lady Michelle Obama, and former US president Barack Obama attend the 25th anniversary commemoration of the September 11, 2001 attacks at the National September 11 Memorial in New York, the US on September 11, 2026. — AFP Bereaved family members were reading out the names of all of those killed, with a bell tolling to mark major moments of the attack, which sparked years of US involvement in Middle East wars and bitter controversy over Washington’s human rights record. “Memorials like this and discussions about those events are an important part of keeping it alive and understanding how we prevent tragedies like this from ever happening again,” said Robert Kafka, a Chicagoan in his 60s visiting the 9/11 Memorial. Alongside the former presidents was Democratic Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the Big Apple’s first Muslim mayor. He faced a well-organised campaign urging him to stay away, spearheaded by the right-wing New York Post and Trump ally and ex- mayor Rudy Giuliani. A petition, which has gathered more than 100,000 signatures, accuses Mamdani of associating with unspecified individuals who are “dismissive of American institutions or insufficiently critical of extremist ideologies”. “It’s concerning to me that the mayor is being treated differently simply because he is Muslim,” city council member Shahana Hanif told CNN . Former US president George W Bush speaks with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani during the 25th anniversary commemoration of the September 11, 2001 attacks at the National September 11 Memorial in New York, the US on September 11, 2026. — AFP Mamdani won plaudits for recently revealing thousands of documents showing what city officials knew about toxicity levels of the air in Lower Manhattan following the attacks. After the initial dust cloud that followed the collapse of the World Trade Centre, months of pollution and lingering dust ensued, causing cancers from which thousands of New Yorkers still suffer today. ‘Toxic air’ Nineteen Al-Qaeda operatives hijacked four airliners on the nearly cloudless autumn day in 2001. Two of the jets slammed into the World Trade Centre’s Twin Towers, causing the iconic 110-storey buildings to collapse. A third plane struck the Pentagon, while a fourth — believed to have been aiming for Congress or the White House — crashed into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers fought back. Beyond those killed on September 11, more than 9,400 other people have died from 9/11-related illnesses, according to the federal program established to provide medical care to those affected. Some 100 million Americans have been born since or are too young to remember the traumatic day. People leave flowers during the 25th anniversary commemoration of the September 11, 2001 attacks at the National September 11 Memorial in New York, the US on September 11, 2026. — AFP Logan Miller, 32, lost his uncle during the attacks, and his grandfather to 9/11-related illness in the aftermath. “I think the next generation just can’t fathom what actually transpired and how someone could be impacted by that, and so I actually find them asking more questions,” he told AFP . Huge crowds were expected to gather in Lower Manhattan for the memorial service. The Secret Service, which protects presidents, erected a security ring around the site of the 9/11 Memorial and Museum. City police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said an anti-drone team would be deployed as a precaution, but stressed there was no intelligence of a specific threat.

Consultations begin to schedule meeting between NA opposition leader and prime minister. Consultations have begun between the offices of the opposition leader and the prime minister to arrange a meeting following Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s letter to National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai regarding the appointment of a new chief election commissioner (CEC), Achakzai said in a statement. A day ago, Dawn , citing an official source, reported that Prime Minister Shehbaz had decided to initiate a dialogue between the government and opposition by inviting Opposition Leader Achakzai for mandatory consultations on the appointment of a new CEC. Earlier in August, Achakzai urged the prime minister in a letter to appoint a new CEC, along with two members representing Sindh and Balochistan. In a social media post on X on Friday, Achakzai said consultations had begun between the offices of the opposition leader and the prime minister following the latter’s letter to schedule a meeting. In a statement, a Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) spokesperson said a meeting was held at the chamber of Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas. The meeting was chaired by Achakzai and attended by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, PTI Secretary General Barrister Salman Akram Raja, Asad Qaiser and others. “The meeting discussed the September 27 protest , with Achakzai and Abbas directing PTI to make full preparations for the protest,” the spokesperson said. He further said that following the prime minister’s letter, consultations had begun between the offices of the opposition leader and the prime minister to arrange a meeting. Last month, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, during an NA session, also stressed the need for political harmony and stability and expressed the desire for the prime minister to initiate dialogue with the opposition by, as a first step, inviting the opposition leader for consultations on the appointment of a new CEC. The five-year term of incumbent CEC Sikandar Sultan Raja expired on Jan 26, 2025. Raja has remained controversial since the ouster of the PTI government in April 2022 over what the opposition called his “support” for the PML-N-led government. One of the main allegations levelled against Raja was that he had deprived PTI of its party symbol , the bat, in the 2024 elections. His critics alleged that the denial of the party symbol was aimed not only at disadvantaging PTI by confusing voters, but also at allowing PTI-backed “independents” to later join the ruling coalition without risking disqualification. They also claimed that the move was intended to deprive PTI of its share of reserved seats. The incumbent CEC Raja, along with Sindh and Balochistan ECP members, have now been in office for over a year after the expiry of their constitutionally mandated five-year terms. The terms of the three officials ended on Jan 26, 2025. Under Article 215(4) of the Constitution, appointments to these posts were required within 45 days after the positions became vacant , i.e., by March 12, 2025. However, a proviso inserted into Article 215(1) through the 26th Constitutional Amendment allows the CEC and members to continue until their successors are appointed. The incumbent CEC and two ECP members are serving under this provision.

Pakistan greenlights $200m ADB loan despite questions over digitalisation project. ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Friday greenlit another $200 million (Rs57bn) loan from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for digitalisation, despite serious questions raised by the Planning Commission. The project was one of seven projects worth Rs116bn cleared by the Central Development Working Party (CDWP) at a meeting presided over by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal. He conditionally cleared the Rs57bn Transforming and Digitalising Revenue Administration (TADRA) project, which aims to increase the tax-to-GDP ratio to 13.5pc by 2029 from 11.1pc at present. The approval comes as the country has already utilised more than $4.7bn in foreign loans aimed at improving revenue collection, while the tax-to-GDP ratio continues to hover around 11pc. The planning minister “recommended the project to the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec), with the condition that the Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), a state-owned think tank, thoroughly review its business model”, an official statement said. It was placed on record that PIDE had already conducted a study on loans taken by the government to reform the energy sector and tax administration, “which indicates that approximately $4.7bn has been obtained from development partners to reform Pakistan’s tax system. “Therefore, the Revenue Division should conduct an impact assessment of previous reform interventions undertaken under the Tax Administration Reforms Programme (TARP), Pakistan Single Window (PSW), Integrated Transit Trade Management System (ITTMS) and Pakistan Raises Revenue Project (PRRP) — the four major loan programmes for the Federal Board of Revenue — to determine the impact of the reforms and value for money.” The project’s clearance was necessary to secure a $200m loan that the ADB’s management had already committed and which required formal approval by its board. The loan is part of the ADB’s Investment Project Financing (IPF) under its Ordinary Capital Resources (OCR) concessional window, or Asian Development Fund, and carries a standard concessional term of 25 years, including a five-year grace period, at an annual interest rate of 1.5pc to 2pc. Based on objections raised by various analytical wings of the Planning Commission and views expressed by PIDE, Iqbal “stressed the need for clearly defined and measurable outcomes, particularly in terms of revenue generation, improvement in the tax-to-GDP ratio and expansion of the taxpayer base”, an official statement said. It added that the FBR had assured that the loan would contribute to increasing the tax-to-GDP ratio to 13.5pc by 2029 and bringing more taxpayers into the tax net. The Planning Commission demanded that, before approving the project and the loan, the FBR should first seek concept clearance on whether the project was synchronised with the FBR’s overall Rs350bn Transformation Plan approved by the federal cabinet. It also sought a matrix of policy actions proposed under the transformation plan, along with the implementation status of each policy action or initiative under previous, ongoing and proposed programmes. The FBR reported that the project was part of its 2024-28 Transformation Plan for accelerating the digitalisation of the revenue administration ecosystem, enhancing operational efficiency, improving taxpayer compliance, ensuring transparent customs clearance and elevating Pakistan’s global competitiveness. The Planning Commission had reservations that the project should not proceed without an impact analysis of already executed projects aimed at reforming and strengthening the FBR’s capacity, a gap analysis of existing facilities, a needs assessment and a feasibility study to determine the requirements of the proposed intervention. It also called for quantifiable results-based measurement indicators (RBMIs) and a plan to ensure the sustainability of the project’s activities after its completion. External experts from the National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences and the National University of Sciences and Technology also highlighted the lack of a gap analysis, a comprehensive data security framework, clarity on the basis of the AI model proposed for system design, and an analysis of the existing system and details of the AI model proposed to be deployed in the new systems. Among other things, the project also seeks to upgrade hardware and software, including existing 850TB servers, to 3PB as data storage requirements are expected to increase following the implementation of video-camera storage and processing systems on production lines in five major sectors, including sugar, cement, tobacco and textiles. The CDWP also recommended the “PakSat-2 Satellite System”, costing Rs37.2bn, to the ECNEC for approval. In June, the CDWP had supported the project in principle to deploy a sovereign, secure and ‘below-internet’ mobile communication network for at least 10,000 government users to address gaps that were causing critical information leakages, but had raised technical questions. The PakSat-2 project is aimed at replacing PakSat-IR, which is set to complete its 15-year operational life later this year. The Planning Commission had advised improving the technical capabilities of the Rs709 million ‘PAKAWAZ Secure Mobile Communication Ecosystem’, which aims to establish a secure mobile communication application capable of supporting video and audio calls, voice and video messages, file and photo sharing, centrally managed contact lists, and text and group messaging, besides application servers, mobile handsets, kill-switch controls and so on. The sources said the National Telecommunication Company (NTC), which had proposed the project, had improved the specifications for an unbreakable security system with maximum integrity to ensure confidentiality, integrity, availability and national data sovereignty. The project is designed to conform to national security requirements by providing an isolated “private 4G LTE Core Network” that is physically or logically air-gapped from the public internet, addressing shortcomings identified after the recent war with India and lessons learnt from other events across the Middle East. Besides referring these two mega projects, worth Rs94.3bn, to Ecnec, the CDWP itself approved five projects with a combined cost of Rs21.59bn. These included the Rs5.015bn “Promotion of Olive Cultivation on Commercial Scale in Pakistan Phase-II”. Phase I was implemented in Kallar Kahar, Islamabad and the wider Potohar belt and is now being expanded to Balochistan and the New Merged Districts. The meeting also approved Rs6bn for a revised project to establish the Dr Ashfaq Ahmad Khan Centre in Basic Sciences across eight national centres, seven of which — covering Artificial Intelligence, Cyber Security, Big Data and Cloud Computing, GIS and Satellite Technology, Automation and Robotics, Applied Mathematics, and Livestock and Genomics — had been completed. The meeting also approved Rs3.623bn for the “Development of Geospatial Complex (Geo-AI Development & Innovation Hub)” for the development of a space programme. Another Rs5.758bn was approved for “Revamping and Refurbishment of Different Facilities at Pakistan Sports Complex (PSC), Islamabad”. A water-sector project titled “Improvement of High Frequency (HF) Radios Network of Water Resources Management Directorate (WRMD), WAPDA”, worth Rs338.179 million, was also approved.

UK lawmakers reject bid to legalise assisted dying. British lawmakers rejected on Friday a proposal to legalise assisted dying for terminally ill people, dealing a major setback to campaigners and bringing the latest effort to change the law to an end. The result leaves Britain’s ban on assisted dying unchanged, extending a decades-long debate over whether terminally ill people should be allowed to end their lives with medical assistance and how vulnerable people could be protected from coercion if the law was changed. Parliament’s lower chamber, the House of Commons, rejected the legislation by 286 votes to 270. The bill would have allowed mentally competent, terminally ill adults in England and Wales with six months or fewer to live to end their lives with medical assistance following approval from a panel of professionals. Bill falls Lauren Edwards, a lawmaker in Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s Labour Party, had brought the legislation back through a mechanism known as a Private Member’s Bill, whereby an individual lawmaker selected in a ballot can try to pass a law independently of the government. “This is a hugely disappointing result not for me but for the many thousands of terminally ill people and their loved ones who were given hope when the Commons voted for this Bill last year,” she said in a statement, referring to the lower house’s previous backing for the legislation. The previous attempt to pass the bill failed after it ran out of time in the House of Lords, the unelected upper chamber. Dignity in Dying, one of the groups campaigning for the bill, also decried Friday’s outcome as “a devastating setback for dying people”, but added: “this issue is not going away. Law change on assisted dying remains a matter of when, not if.” Since Friday’s measure failed at its first parliamentary hurdle, it cannot be revived during the current legislative session, which is expected to run until the spring of next year. Gordon Macdonald, chief executive of campaign group Care Not Killing, welcomed the result, saying lawmakers had recognised concerns that changing the law could put pressure on vulnerable people to end their lives prematurely. “Our current laws protect vulnerable people and (members of parliament) have rightly said they do not need changing; it’s time to move beyond this debate and fix palliative care,” Macdonald added. Concerns over safeguards Prime Minister Andy Burnham has previously said the debate over legalising assisted dying should wait until Britain’s palliative and adult social care systems had been improved, though his government remained neutral on the legislation and allowed lawmakers to vote according to their conscience. Burnham did not take part in Friday’s vote. The latest legislation was identical to the bill approved by lawmakers last year, a move supporters hoped would eventually allow them to use the Parliament Acts, which give the lower house supremacy over the upper chamber to overcome opposition in the House of Lords if peers again refused to pass it. During Friday’s debate, bill sponsor Edwards said improving end-of-life choice did not have to come at the expense of palliative care. “We can and we should do both,” she said. Questions over safeguards for vulnerable people remained central to the debate, with opponents arguing the bill could expose some terminally ill people to pressure to end their lives. Parliament also rejected a similar attempt to legalise assisted dying in 2015. A poll published by Ipsos on Monday showed two in three Britons supported the legalisation of assisted dying in principle, though in some cases, that backing hinged on additional funding being provided for palliative care.

India's Modi stresses need to protect navigation, seafarers in talks with Iran's Pezeshkian. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Friday and underscored the need to protect the freedom of navigation and commerce, and the safety and well-being of seafarers, India’s foreign ministry said. The talks were held on the eve of the annual summit of Brics leaders in the Indian capital, which will see the participation of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian, among others. India is walking a tightrope in the conflict, boasting historical and cultural ties with Iran, strong, strategic relations with Israel and close friendships with Arab countries, where millions of its nationals live and work. The South Asian nation has been particularly affected by attacks on vessels transiting the region, which have killed at least 10 Indians. “The prime minister [Modi] reiterated India’s consistent position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy,” the ministry said in a statement. “He also underscored the need for continued efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in the region, safeguarding freedom of navigation and commerce, and the safety and well-being of seafarers,” it added. This was the second meeting between the leaders in as many weeks. They last held talks on August 31, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, where Pezeshkian told Modi that Tehran wanted a negotiated solution to its conflict with the US. New Delhi has condemned Tehran’s attacks on its Gulf neighbours, energy infrastructure in the region, and on ships that have led to the deaths of crew members but, in a surprise move at the Bishkek summit, signed a joint declaration condemning the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran and Western sanctions. Earlier, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin began talks in New Delhi on Friday, their second meeting in two weeks, which is expected to focus on trade, energy and defence ties between the two countries, which have long been friends. Modi and Putin were expected to discuss cooperation between the two countries in civil nuclear energy, fertilisers, defence, critical minerals, manufacturing, railways, and steel, an Indian source said. The two leaders met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31, where Modi told Putin that the war in Ukraine needed to end for humanity’s sake and that New Delhi would support every peace effort to stop the fighting. India, along with China, is one of the biggest buyers of Russian oil, which is seen as helping Moscow replenish its budget since it sent tens of thousands of troops into Ukraine in 2022 and was hit with sweeping Western sanctions. India has, however, sought to resist the pressure, saying its large population and economy need secure, affordable and reliable energy supplies. New Delhi has also said that the Ukraine conflict can be resolved only through dialogue and diplomacy and not by some countries stopping energy, metal or fertiliser trade with Russia. Russia’s share of Indian crude imports rose in 2026, reaching a record 51 per cent in July, as disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies increased Indian refiners’ reliance on Russian oil. That share likely moderated in August as China stepped up Russian oil purchases, Indian media reported. Putin visited India in December 2025 as well for the annual India-Russia summit and the two countries agreed to expand their trade and defence relationship. India prepares for Brics Leaders from Iran were also in India for talks on Friday, ahead of a Brics summit dominated by conflict and economic challenges. “One should engage in debate and friendship only with the virtuous, and nothing whatsoever with the unvirtuous,” Modi wrote on Friday, in a social media message in Sanskrit to welcome leaders to the 11-nation summit. Posters of a beaming Modi line streets across New Delhi, with heavy deployments of security forces across the capital and widespread traffic restrictions. Wars in the Middle East and Ukraine , as well as global trade turbulence and oil are expected on the agenda at the two-day annual summit that opens on Saturday, when Xi is set to arrive. It will be Xi’s first visit to India since 2019, and marks the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the rival neighbours, six years after a deadly military clash along their disputed Tibetan border. Ties between the nuclear-armed Asian giants have been warming again, with flights, visas and high-level contacts gradually being restored. “China stands ready to work with India … by strengthening communication, enhancing cooperation, and properly handling differences,” Beijing’s foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said Friday. A woman walks past country flags outside Bharat Mandapam, the venue of the upcoming BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, on September 10, 2026. — Reuters Deep mistrust remains, with their contested Himalayan frontier, a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry still complicating ties. Dozens of Tibetans protested in New Delhi on Friday — exiles, like their Buddhist leader the Dalai Lama, who has lived in India since fleeing a Chinese crackdown in 1959 — waving placards against Xi’s visit. Brics was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who arrived in New Delhi on Friday and will hold talks with Modi, said that “Brics was established to counter unilateralism”, according to Tehran’s IRNA news agency. This handout photograph taken and released by the Indian Press Information Bureau (PIB) on September 11, 2026 shows Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian disembarking from his plane after arriving at Palam Air Base in New Delhi. —PIB via AFP ‘Fault line’ As well as Iran, Brics includes Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates — countries with sharply differing positions on the war launched by the United States and Israel in February. All three have been admitted to the group in recent years, joining founding member states that include India, China and Russia. “The Gulf conflict is going to be the central fault line this time during the Brics summit,” said Harsh V. Pant of India’s Observer Research Foundation. “What was seen until last year as an achievement — the expansion of Brics — today looks like a big constraint on Brics,” Pant said. Pezeshkian’s participation — his first visit to India as Iranian president — will put the Middle East conflict firmly on the agenda. “The war in Iran will provide a stern test of the group’s cohesion,” said Shilan Shah of Capital Economics, noting the failure of the Brics foreign ministers to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May. UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is also expected, as is Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan, and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

PM Shehbaz orders no more than two hours of loadshedding across country. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday ordered that there should be no loadshedding for more than two hours in any area of the country, according to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The premier was chairing a meeting on electricity load management when he issued the instructions, expressing displeasure over increasing loadshedding nationwide, the statement added. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema, Climate Change Minister Mushtaq Malik, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, Power Minister Sardar Awais Leghari, Adviser to the Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah and other relevant senior government officials were in attendance. “The prime minister said that no area should experience load shedding for more than two hours,” the statement read. The meeting was informed that the supply of regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) had been affected by the ongoing situation in the Middle East and tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. This had caused a reduction in electricity generation, which in turn led to load management to “maintain a balance between demand and supply”, the PMO said. PM Shehbaz ordered immediate measures to address the disruption in RLNG supplies. Keeping the situation in the region and future requirements in view, he made it clear that all available resources “should be utilised effectively so that no area experiences electricity load shedding for more than two hours”. Furthermore, the prime minister ordered the formation of Consumer Grievance Redressal Committees at the distribution company level within a week to address public complaints related to electricity transmission and power supply issues. He also directed that public representatives be included in these redressal committees. The US-Iran war, which began on February 28, has disrupted the supply of RLNG cargoes from Qatar via the Strait of Hormuz. This resulted in the government purchasing five expensive cargoes from the spot market in July, with the sale price of RLNG witnessing the biggest-ever increase in the commodity’s decade-long history. The cost of RLNG-based power generation surged by a record 242 per cent to Rs47.4 per unit in July, from less than Rs14 in April.

GB election tribunal suspends IPP's Imam Malik's membership, orders recount of postal ballots in GBA-16 Diamer-II. GILGIT: A Gilgit-Baltistan election tribunal on Friday suspended the GB Assembly membership of Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party’s (IPP) Imam Malik from GBA-16 Diamer-II, directing the returning officer (RO) of the constituency to complete the verification and counting of postal ballot papers by September 16. Election tribunal judge Mushtaq Ahmed conducted a hearing on a petition filed by PPP candidate Attaullah Khan challenging the general election result in the constituency. Khan, through his counsel Advocate Islamuddin, had challenged the issuance of the election result of GBA-16 Diamer-II after the GB general elections in June. The petitioner argued that the RO of the constituency had issued Form 49 without counting the postal ballots. Subsequently, the GB chief election commissioner (CEC) had declared Malik, then an independent candidate, the winner from the constituency. He later joined the IPP. The petitioner pleaded with the tribunal to declare the result of the constituency null and void and the notification declaring the returned candidate illegal. He also requested the tribunal to issue a consolidated result after counting the postal ballots. After hearing arguments from both sides and considering reports from the CEC, Justice Ahmed issued the verdict in the case on Friday. The judgement said the RO had no authority to issue a provisional consolidated result. The CEC had also committed a serious error by issuing a declaration based on the provisional consolidated result, it added. “The preliminary order is issued to ensure strict compliance with the mandatory statutory requirement under Section 95 of the Elections Act 2017 read with Rule 85 of the Elections Rules 2017, for the issuance of the final consolidated result of the constituency GBA-16 Diamer-II,” Justice Ahmed wrote in his judgement. The judgement directed the RO of the constituency to open the sealed parcel containing the postal ballot papers in the presence of the parties or their duly authorised agents. The order said: “To ensure transparency and judicial oversight, Fahad Bin Naqeeb, a senior civil judge, Gilgit, and Raja Mir, assistant registrar, GB Chief Court, along with the assisting team of this tribunal, shall remain present throughout the result consolidation proceedings.” The election tribunal judge also directed the police to make stringent and foolproof security arrangements at the venue. It added that upon completion of the verification and counting of postal ballot papers, the RO would prepare and issue the final consolidated result, Form-49, and submit it to the CEC. It said that, on the basis of the final consolidated result, the CEC would issue a fresh declaration of the returned candidate. The order said the entire exercise should be concluded within five days, including Sunday, September 13, from the date of the order. The order declared the final consolidated result of the constituency, dated June 16, 2025, illegal for not including the postal ballot papers. It also suspended Malik’s membership of GBA-16 Diamer-II until completion of the final consolidated result.

Razaullah heroics deny England quickfire win in third Test against Pakistan. Debutant Razaullah launched a remarkable late salvo as Pakistan finally showed some fight on Friday to keep England waiting for a clean sweep in their three-Test series. The fast bowler came to the crease with the tourists on the brink of defeat in the third Test at Edgbaston but clubbed nine sixes in an astonishing innings of 81 off 63 balls. Fellow paceman Mohammad Abbas also joined the party as the pair took the score from 318-8 to 439-9, with England seemingly powerless to stop the carnage late on the third day. It means the teams will have to come back on Saturday, with the home home side needing to score 130 to wrap up a 3-0 win after dominating the series. Earlier, Shan Masood scored 95 and captain Babar Azam made 76 as much-changed Pakistan passed 200 for the first time in the series at the sixth attempt. Pakistan, facing a first-innings deficit of 320, lost two wickets without scoring a single run on Thursday but opener Azan Awais and the experienced Shan took the score to 125. Their partnership was broken in Friday’s morning session when Azan was caught down the leg side by stand-in wicket-keeper Jordan Cox off the bowling of spinner Dan Lawrence for 59, bringing Babar to the crease. Shan was in sight of an eighth Test hundred when he fell to a sensational slip catch by Dan Lawrence off the bowling of Gus Atkinson. Babar, who missed the first Test with an injured hand, batted fluently but got a feather of a touch to a Josh Tongue delivery, with Cox taking the catch. Saud Shakeel (29) was next to go, caught by Emilio Gay at short leg while trying to fend off a Jofra Archer bouncer, while two more Cox catches accounted for Ghazi Ghori and Mohammad Imran. Fireworks But Pakistan were not finished as Abbas joined Razaullah at the crease for their show of evening fireworks. Debutant paceman Razaullah showed his intent early, clubbing three sixes off Atkinson in four balls and the pair brought up their fifty partnership off just 57 balls. Inspired, Abbas, with a previous top Test score of 29, smashed Ollie Robinson for six. Razaullah reached an astonishing 50 off 43 balls with a fifth six, this time off Archer, repeating the dose the following ball to leave the England man shaking his head. Abbas was eventually caught by Atkinson off the bowling of Tongue for 42, ending a partnership of 121 for the ninth wicket. Razaullah had by now removed his helmet to face Lawrence, launching him into the stands to move into the 80s in the final over. He survived an lbw on review but was stumped by Cox off the next ball for 81 as the spectators applauded him off. In total he hit four fours and nine sixes to go with his four wickets in England’s first innings. England bowled Pakistan out for a meagre 133 on the opening day before making 453 at a brisk pace. Joe Root’s side have dominated the series, winning the first game by an innings and 103 runs and the second by 194 runs. Pakistan released seven players and sacked head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul after their defeat in the second Test, making four changes to their side in Birmingham.

Under fire Imam, Rizwan barred from playing in President's Trophy. Dropped Pakistan internationals Imam-ul-Haq and Mohammad Rizwan have been barred from playing in the President’s Trophy Grade-I domestic first-class tournament, which starts across four venues on Saturday. Dawn understands that the duo, who were questioned by the National Cybercrime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Thursday following a complaint lodged by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), have been restricted from joining their respective teams until the probe against them is settled. Imam was named captain of the Oil and Gas Development Company (OGDCL) side, while Rizwan was included as vice-captain of the Sui Northern Gas Pipelines (SNGPL) team in the squads announced by the PCB on Thursday. According to sources, the two players would not have been eligible to play in the opening round of the tournament anyway as they did not participate in a mandatory fitness test held ahead of the competition. However, the departments concerned have reportedly been told that the two players should not be allowed to play “until the end of the investigation”. The development comes after Imam and Rizwan appeared before the NCCIA in connection with an investigation into alleged leaks from Pakistan’s dressing room during the ongoing Test tour of England. The two were among seven players who were called back home following Pakistan’s defeats in the first two Tests, leaving England with an unassailable lead in the three-match series. While five players were dropped for cricketing reasons, Imam and Rizwan’s withdrawal from the Pakistan squad was followed by reports that their mobile phones had been confiscated by PCB officials. The board subsequently confirmed the launch of an “internal inquiry” against the two players. Earlier, national selector and PCB director of high performance Aaqib Javed had said Imam would also be investigated for not coming out to bat during either innings of Pakistan’s second Test against England at Lord’s, which the visitors lost by 194 runs. Aaqib’s comments came in the aftermath of the PCB’s wholesale changes following the second Test, which also saw the sacking of head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul, amid speculation that Imam had been fit enough to bat. On Thursday, a PCB spokesperson acknowledged reports regarding an NCCIA probe involving certain cricketers, but said the board would not comment while the inquiry was ongoing. However, a source privy to the development told Dawn that both cricketers appeared at the NCCIA office in Lahore after being summoned through notices and were questioned by investigators for around four hours. According to the source, both players told investigators that their cellphones were already with the NCCIA and that the agency could carry out forensic examinations of the devices. Both players have also reportedly sought more time to submit written responses to the investigating agency. “The inquiry will focus on alleged leaks from the dressing room during the England series,” the source had said.

'Decisive phase': JI chief announces Islamabad march on Sept 20 against petroleum levy. GUJRANWALA: Jamaat-i-Islami chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Friday announced that the party would march towards Islamabad on September 20 against the petroleum levy , warning the government that the protest would enter its “decisive phase” on the streets of the federal capital if the levy was not withdrawn before the march. Addressing a public gathering in Gujranwala, Rehman said caravans from across the country would converge on Islamabad and urged the “Form-47 rulers” to “read the writing on the wall” and provide immediate relief to the people. “If the petroleum levy is not abolished before the long march begins, the decision will be made on the streets of Islamabad,” he said, adding that failure to meet public demands would force the JI to launch a movement to bring down the government. The government levies Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. The gathering was also addressed by JI Central Punjab Emir Javed Qasuri, Gujranwala Emir Mazhar Randhawa and other party leaders. Leaders of the JI Women’s Wing also attended the event. The JI’s sit-ins against the petroleum levy in Lahore, Peshawar, Karachi and dozens of other locations across the country entered their 27th day on Friday. Rehman also announced that he would address a women’s public gathering in Islamabad on Saturday and said the ongoing sit-ins would be expanded. Earlier, he chaired a meeting of party leaders from across the country at Mansoorah in Lahore, where the party discussed the next phase of its protest movement. Speaking in Gujranwala, Rehman said the JI had emerged as a source of hope for the people and added that rulers who had deprived the country of its rights for 79 years had now realised the party’s growing strength. He criticised the dominance of bureaucracy, feudal landlords and influential families in the country and said the working class was suffering while children were being forced into labour and deprived of education. The JI leader also criticised the provincial government over cases of violence and exploitation against women, alleging that around 6,500 such cases had been registered in Punjab but convictions had been secured in only a few. He challenged Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to provide the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) with a complete account of her income and expenditure after her recent remarks about travelling to London on a government aircraft at her own expense. The JI chief alleged that the Sharif and Zardari families were among those responsible for the exploitation of poor people and added that more than 40 per cent of Punjab’s population was living in poverty. Rehman also criticised the government over petroleum levy collections , claiming Rs1,567 billion had been collected from the public under the levy. He questioned why the government was imposing “jagga tax” on citizens while basic healthcare and education remained inaccessible to millions. He said successive governments since the 1990s had benefited independent power producers (IPPs), questioning why rulers were collecting additional taxes from citizens instead of reducing their own expenditures. Rehman also questioned the federal government’s continued budget allocations after the 18th Amendment transferred several powers and departments to the provinces. He further called for an end to interest-based financial practices, citing a ruling by the Federal Shariat Court, and said even a partial reduction in interest payments could save the national exchequer thousands of billions of rupees. The party chief said the JI had raised these issues during talks with the government but added that the authorities had failed to provide satisfactory answers. “If the rulers have no answers, the people will now demand answers from them,” he said. On August 16, the JI announced sit-ins in all the provincial capitals of Pakistan against the petroleum levy. It had also called a nationwide strike on September 3.

Fatima Sana's all-round effort in vain as Sri Lanka down Pakistan in Women's Asia Cup semi-final. Pakistan captain Fatima Sana’s all-round effort went in vain as Sri Lanka defeated Pakistan in a Women’s Asia Cup semi-final for the third consecutive edition on Friday, chasing down their 131-run target with seven balls to spare to set up a final against India. Fatima scored an unbeaten 47 off 36 balls and took four wickets, but Sri Lanka reached 134-6 with Harshita Samarawickrama leading the chase with 36 off 31 balls. Sri Lanka opted to bowl after winning the toss, meaning Pakistan batted first for the fourth consecutive match in the tournament. Pakistan also fielded an unchanged XI for the fourth successive game. Pakistan made a slow start, with opener Muneeba Ali falling to Sugandika Kumari in the second over, sending a simple catch to mid-off. Shawaal Zulfiqaar then accelerated, hitting Mithali Ayodhya for two fours and a six in the next over. She then cleared long-on off Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu for six, but fell to the same bowler off the next delivery while attempting to play the ball fine. Wicket-keeper Kaushini Nuthyangana completed a sharp catch. Ayesha Zafar joined Gul Feroza but lasted only eight balls, scoring seven before edging Athapaththu to the wicketkeeper while attempting a cut. Sadaf Shamas was then stumped off Chamudi Praboda for eight off 11 balls, bringing Fatima to the crease. Fatima and Feroza consolidated the innings with a 40-run partnership before Feroza was caught by Athapaththu at long-off off Praboda. Fatima and Tuba Hassan then added 38 in the final four overs to take Pakistan to 130-6. Fatima battled cramps in the Dubai heat to remain unbeaten on 47, hitting boundaries off both Athapaththu and Kavisha Dilhari, while Tuba scored 12 off 10 balls. Fatima strikes early Fatima made an immediate impact with the ball, taking two wickets from two deliveries in her first over to leave Sri Lanka reeling at 5-2. Athapaththu was caught at deep backward square before Sanjana Kavindi was dismissed off the next ball, sending a leading edge to midwicket. Hasini Perera and Imesha Dulani then steadied the innings, rotating the strike to take Sri Lanka to 31 before Sadia Iqbal struck. Perera miscued a delivery into the air, with Ayesha Zafar holding on to a well-judged catch. Umm-e-Hani then removed Dulani to reduce Sri Lanka to 33-4. However, Samarawickrama and Dilhari put Sri Lanka back in control with a 67-run partnership, taking the score to 100-4. The pair took the attack to Pakistan’s spinners, scoring briskly against Tuba Hassan, Ayesha Zafar and Nashra Sandhu. Fatima returned to strike twice in her third over and complete her four-wicket haul. She dismissed Samarawickrama off the first ball of the 17th over before trapping Dilhari leg-before wicket off the final delivery. Two boundaries between those wickets, however, ensured Sri Lanka remained in control of the chase. Kaushini Nuthyangana and Nilakshika Silva then took Sri Lanka over the line. Nuthyangana hit the first six of her international career before Silva sealed victory with a four, both boundaries coming off Fatima. The victory marked Sri Lanka’s third consecutive Asia Cup semi-final win over Pakistan, following their victories in the 2022 and 2024 editions. “We have good players. If we can execute our plans in the final, we can beat any team,” Athapaththu said after the match. Fatima, who was named player of the match for her all-round performance, said lapses in the field had cost Pakistan despite what she considered a defendable total. She also said the team needed to improve as a batting unit. Sri Lanka will meet India in the final on Sunday in a repeat of the previous edition’s title clash.

Action ordered against PIA, ASF staff for misbehaving with lawmakers. ISLAMABAD: The Senate Rules of Procedure and Privile­ges Committee on Friday directed Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) and the Airport Security Force (ASF) to initiate disciplinary action against staff members accused of misbehaving with senators, saying such conduct damages the credibility of government’s institutions. Chaired by Senator Syed Waqar Mehdi, the meeting at Parliament House took up three privilege motions related to alleged misconduct by PIA cabin crew and ASF personnel. The committee considered a privilege motion moved by Senator Bilal Ahmed Khan Mandokhail regarding alleged misbehaviour by a PIA cabin crew member on flight PK-326 from Quetta to Islamabad on February 7, 2026. The matter had earlier come before the committee, which recommended that the official concerned contact the senator and apologise. Senator Mandokhail informed the panel that no PIA official had reached him, and demanded disciplinary action, including dismissal. Expressing concern over the staff’s conduct, Chairman Mehdi cited a recent social media report about alleged cigarette smuggling at Multan Airport. “If true, this is very unfortunate,” he said, adding that such behaviour by PIA staff and officials “tarnishes PIA’s reputation”. The committee recommended that PIA initiate departmental disciplinary action against the cabin crew member in accordance with the law, and disposed of the privilege motion. The panel also took up a privilege motion by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri regarding alleged misbehaviour by ASF officials during check-in for Emirates flight EK-601 on July 24, 2026. Senator Zehri told the committee that during travel to London, an ASF official searched her hand-carry bag and questioned her about the cash she was carrying. She said she offered to go to a side office to count foreign currency as per procedure, but the official instead opened her bag at the desk where three other bags were already open for inspection. “I asked that my bag be taken to the side room, but the duty officer behaved inappropriately and did not listen,” she said. “If a parliamentarian can be treated like this, one can only imagine how ordinary citizens are treated.” A senior ASF officer expressed regret and apologised, assuring the committee the matter would be taken up with the relevant authorities and Pakistan Customs. The committee recommended that ASF personnel be given pro­per training in dealing with the public. Senator Mehdi direc­ted that lower-ranking ASF staff be trained in better public conduct. The committee further directed that an inquiry be completed within 15 days and that the officer found responsible be produced before the next meeting. Published in Dawn, September 12th, 2026

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs375.82 per litre while HSD will cost Rs403.32 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable from Sept 12 (Saturday) to Sept 14 (Monday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

KP Assembly seeks Article 6 action against Punjab CM. • Passes resolution against Maryam Nawaz; terms her remarks about ‘security threats from neighbouring provinces’ harmful to national unity • PML-N claims her statement is being misread, misrepresented PESHAWAR: After suspending the day’s agenda, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly on Friday passed a majority resolution seeking action against Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz under Article 6 of the Constitution over her remarks that Punjab faced greater security threats from “neighbouring provinces than neighbouring countries” and that terrorism entered the province through its borders. The resolution, moved by Law Minister Aftab Alam Afridi during a sitting chaired by Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, said such statements could harm national unity, spread hatred among the provinces and undermine the federation. It paid tribute to those who had laid down their lives for the country in the war against terrorism, saying the menace was a challenge for the entire country and could be defeated only through joint efforts. Earlier, Housing Minister Amjad Ali said the Punjab chief minister’s statement was not directed against PTI alone but against the entire province, calling it shameful and insulting and saying it reflected her arrogance. He said the Punjab chief minister had undermined the state’s narrative as the state had, for the past two years, been pointing fingers at India over terrorism in Pakistan. “She must apologise on the floor of the house for saying that Punjab faces threats not from India but from other provinces,” he said. Mr Ali also questioned who had trained and financially supported the Taliban, turned KP into a battlefield and supported the then Mujahideen for 45 years, adding that as soon as the US lost interest, the “Mujahideen” came to be called terrorists. Information Minister Shafi Jan claimed that the Punjab chief minister had given a clean chit to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and questioned whether the army’s narrative, being built for the past four years, was correct. He told the house that the statement had been issued intentionally and could be used against Pakistan in the International Court of Justice. He added that when a military operation was launched against militants in KP and locals fled their homes, then Punjab chief minister Shehbaz Sharif had blocked the entry of displaced persons into Punjab. He also alleged that PTI was not involved in the May 9 riots , but those who benefited from the situation were responsible. The speaker then asked Mr Afridi to read out the oath of judges and questioned whether judges were adhering to it. Mr Afridi said any judge who followed the oath was either superseded or transferred. Mr Afridi also read out the oath of the chief election commissioner and said the incumbent chief election commissioner’s tenure had ended on Jan 26, 2025, but he remained in office and was being facilitated. On the speaker’s orders, Mr Afridi also read out the oath of the armed forces, after which the chair questioned whether the three institutions were adhering to their respective oaths. “Are courts delivering justice? Is the ECP performing its duties? Are the armed forces abiding by their oath?” the speaker asked, to which lawmakers replied in the negative. Higher Education Minister Meena Khan told the house that the issue was not about any individual but concerned three provinces. “We are fighting the state’s war,” he said. ANP’s Muhammad Nisar said the statement was an insult to the people of KP and Balochistan. “This war has been imposed on us to appease the Americans,” he said, adding that Punjab had not felt its impact. He questioned why, if security forces could maintain law and order in Punjab, they could not do the same in KP. However, PML-N’s Amna Sardar said her leader had never named Pakhtuns in her statement and accused the treasury benches of spreading hatred. She said the word “Pakhtun” had been added to the statement by treasury members and argued that Maryam Nawaz’s remarks were being misread and misrepresented. Published in Dawn, September 12th, 2026

Nepra okays $58bn 11-year power plan amid reservations. ISLAMABAD: In a controversial decision, the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Friday approved the contentious Integrated System Plan (ISP) 2025, entailing a total investment of about $58 billion in the power generation and transmission sectors over 11 years. In a 45-page decision conditionally approving the 11-year (2025-35) planning document, all three members, including the Nepra chairman, wrote more than 12 pages of dissenting or separate advisory notes while questioning the grounds for the exclusion and inclusion of major projects and bypassing the Council of Common Interests (CCI) — the constitutional forum dealing with such matters, including the national energy policy and plan. “The Authority hereby approves the ISP-2025, to the extent of Revised Base/Recommended Case of IGCEP-2025 (excluding Battery Energy Storage System-BESS and K-Electric Ltd-KEL transmission line in 2028) together with the revised scope of Transmission System Expansion Plan (TSEP-2025), subject to redressal of the observations of the Authority,” the Nepra decision said. It also placed on record contradictory statements by two related organisations — the Independent System and Market Operator (ISMO) and Power Planning and Monitoring Company (PPMC) — under the power division. Members question project changes, CCI bypass Nepra also expressed displeasure over changes to the 10-year investment plan on the advice of a technical committee constituted by the power division, noting that changes to the National Electricity Policy or National Electricity Plan could not be dictated by a technical committee or the power division without going back to the CCI. Nepra noted that ISP-2025 superseded earlier Integrated Generation Cap­acity Exp­ansion Plans and considered three principal demand forecast scenarios — high growth, medium growth and low growth — one of which was treated as the business-as-usual (BAU) scenario. The corresponding cumulative average GDP gro­wth assumptions are 6.37pc, 4.95pc and 3.52pc. The low-growth, or business-as-usual, scenario based on the Rationalised Capacity Addition (RCA) assumption was adopted as the reference case for generation expansion planning. It envisages capacity addition of 26,045MW — 17,485MW committed and 8,560MW optimised — along with the retirement of 2,577MW of existing capacity, resulting in total installed capacity of 62,657MW. This also includes 8,120MW of net metering. The total projected cost of the additional capacity is $47.08bn. Sherry Rehman raises alarm over child abuse crisis. • Says 1,914 cases of violence and abuse against children were reported from January to June 2026 • Urges speedy trials, strict punishment for perpetrators ISLAMABAD: PPP Vice President Senator Sherry Rehman on Friday expressed deep concern over what she called a “serious child protection crisis” in Pakistan, citing 1,914 reported cases of violence and abuse against children between January and June 2026. “There can be no impunity for those who prey on children,” she said in a statement. “The scale of these cases is deeply disturbing. We are talking about children who should be protected by their families, communities and the state, yet are instead becoming victims of violence and abuse. This cannot be treated as a series of isolated incidents. It requires an urgent and coordinated response.” Punjab accounts for 80pc of cases Senator Rehman noted that 80 per cent of the reported cases were from Punjab, raising questions about the effectiveness of existing child protection mechanisms. “These figures must prompt a closer examination of whether children are able to report abuse safely, whether protection institutions are adequately equipped, and whether perpetrators are being effectively brought to justice,” she said. She said the most disturbing aspect was that 43pc of the accused were known to the victims, while nearly 45pc of incidents reportedly took place inside children’s own homes. “The home is supposed to be the first line of protection for a child. When abuse takes place behind those doors, we have to ask very difficult questions about vigilance, safeguards and accountability within families and communities,” she added. According to the data cited by Ms Rehman, 57pc of cases were reported from urban areas and 43pc from rural areas. “Child abuse does not belong to one class, one locality or one community. It is a societal problem. We have to build systems of protection that work everywhere and for every child,” she said. The senator said the registration of 89pc of reported cases with the police was encouraging, but stressed that registration must be followed by investigation and prosecution. “Registration is only the beginning. Every reported case must be investigated promptly, prosecuted effectively and pursued to its logical conclusion. Where guilt is established, perpetrators must face strict and exemplary punishment under the law,” she said. ‘Speedy trials’ Ms Rehman urged the higher judiciary to ensure speedy trials in cases involving serious crimes against children, warning that delays could deepen a sense of impunity and further traumatise victims. “Justice delayed in cases of violence against children is not simply a procedural failure. It can become another form of injustice for the child,” she added. ‘Shared responsibility’ She said protecting children was a shared responsibility of the state and society, and urged parents and guardians to remain vigilant. “Parents must remain alert, but we cannot place the entire burden of protection on families. The state has a constitutional and moral responsibility to create an environment where children can live without fear of violence, exploitation or abuse,” she added. “If, as a state, we cannot guarantee our innocent children their fundamental right to safety and protection, then we must ask ourselves what kind of future we are building. Protecting that right is not optional; it is a fundamental responsibility of the state and society,” Senator Rehman concluded. Published in Dawn, September 12th, 2026

Group in Yemen used Claude AI for missile projects, Anthropic says. • Identifies cell of threat actors running three weapons development programmes • Claims it banned accounts as soon as it detected illegal activity PARIS: A group in Yemen attempted to use Anthropic’s Claude chatbot to build guided rockets and missiles, the US firm has revealed, as Houthi forces are on the offensive in the country. In a report published on Thursday on how it had prevented illegal uses of Claude in several countries, the leading US AI firm said it had “identified a cell of threat actors based in northern Yemen running three weapons development programmes”. Those were “a guided rocket that used a commodity phone-class flight computer with final-phase homing guidance; a multi-stage ballistic missile with a stated range goal above 2,000 kilometres (1,250 miles); and a multi-variant missile… that included a hypersonic glide vehicle variant”. The cell used Claude to develop guidance, navigation and control software for the airborne weapons that would have otherwise required a team of engineers. “We do not have evidence the actors succeeded in fielding an operational device; but they did test-fire a guided rocket,” Anthropic said. “This field test appears to have failed: within hours, the actors returned to Claude to work out why it failed.” Anthropic said it had banned the relevant accounts as soon as it had detected the illegal activity. While the company did not identify the actors in question, it is likely to involve the Houthis, who control much of northern Yemen, including the capital, Sanaa. The revelation comes at a time when the Houthi rebels have launched a wide-ranging offensive across the country towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait, which connects Europe to Asia. On Friday, the Houthis claimed control of a Red Sea island in the middle of the Bab al-Mandeb shipping lane, completing their push to control the area. Meanwhile, Anthropic also broke up attempts to use its Claude models to develop biological weapons and carry out a suspected Russia-linked cyber espionage campaign against Ukraine. It accused Chinese competitors of hacking attempts aimed at extracting Claude’s capabilities in its report. Two Anthropic researchers warned this week that rapidly progressing artificial intelligence could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future.
